summary: B follows the frozen contract much more closely: it adds the exact convenience API, validates inputs, uses the established multipart helper, and delegates to FilesService.Add without changing Add itself.
reasons: B calls multipartbody.NewFile("file", fileName, content), satisfying the required multipart field, filename, buffering helper, and source-reader error propagation.
B routes the encoded body through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), preserving existing option handling, request construction, decoding, and errors.
B explicitly validates both an empty filename and nil content before constructing or sending a request.

A materially changes FilesService.Add by eagerly reading and buffering every caller-provided body, contrary to the requirement to preserve its existing behavior and avoid unrelated retry refactoring affecting the lower-level API contract snapshot semantics and memory use profile may shift for custom bodies in ways callers did not opt into, including very large or streaming multipart bodies.. Therefore A is not preferred. This sentence mixed? Need clean. A also bypasses Add from Upload via private add, directly violating required delegation path.
risks_a: Changes Add semantics and memory usage by unconditionally consuming the entire reader before request construction.
Upload calls a new private add method instead of the required existing Add method.
Documentation advertises the out-of-scope Add behavior change as a feature, making the contract violation intentional and externally visible becoming externally committed behavior.
risks_b: Visible tests omit the contract-required empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error cases.

The retry test checks only that two requests occur; it neither inspects the multipart body on both attempts nor uses a clearly one-shot/streamed source, so replay verification is weaker than A's test.
The combined validation error is less specific than separate filename/content errors, though the contract does not prescribe exact messages.
